sections.heading: C — Traffic signal decisions
sections.markdown:
## C — Traffic signal decisions

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
Traffic signals, roadside signs and pavement markings are forms of traffic control. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
Drivers must follow traffic directions given by law enforcement personnel, highway workers or school crossing guards. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
A green traffic light allows travel only when proceeding is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
In the usual vertical traffic signal, green is below yellow and red is above yellow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A02
A steady green light allows entry into the intersection while required yielding duties still apply. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A02
When a stopped driver receives a green light, traffic already crossing must clear before the driver moves. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A02
A green arrow authorizes a turn in its indicated direction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A02
A left turn on a steady green light is permitted only when safe, with oncoming traffic having priority. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A02
Before turning left on green, check for signs that forbid the turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A02
During either a right turn or a left turn, watch for pedestrians crossing your path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A02
A steady yellow light warns of the coming red light and requires stopping when stopping is safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A02
A driver already inside the intersection when yellow appears should continue through instead of stopping there. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A02
A flashing yellow light calls for reduced speed and cautious travel. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
A yellow arrow ends protected turning time; if turning in its direction, prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A02
A steady red light requires a stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A02
A bright blinking light located inside a red signal is an added warning that the red light requires stopping. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

Misconceptions: a green light still requires yielding where the handbook specifies it.
Mnemonics: flashing yellow means caution; flashing red means stop.
Glossary: a protected arrow controls a direction of travel; a steady light and a flashing light carry different instructions.
Dynamic facts: obey the signal and any posted restriction present at the intersection.
